proposals.expected_signal: If popularity bias is masking ranking headroom on ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10, degree-aware hard negatives should improve top-10 discrimination over uniform sampling without changing the frozen protocol;
proposals.failure_mode: Hard negatives may over-focus on popular items, collapsing personalization and yielding no gain or slight regression versus the simpler baseline.
proposals.hypothesis: A LightGCN variant trained with sampled unobserved negatives biased toward mid/high-degree items, plus inverse-degree constraint weighting on positives, will produce a structurally distinct signal by forcing finer preference separation among competitive items while damping pure popularity reinforcement.
